rows.note: Use 知 as the all-purpose verb for knowing facts, being aware of something, or having information.

example.english: I know he’ll come back tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zi1 keoi5 ting1 jat6 wui5 faan1 lei4

rows.note: Use 識 when you are acquainted or familiar with a person, place, or thing.

example.english: I know this restaurant; the food is really good.
example.traditional: 我識呢間餐廳，啲嘢食好好食。
example.jyutping: ngo5 sik1 ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 je5 sik6 hou2 hou2 sik6

rows.note: Use 明 when “know” means understand or grasp how something works.

example.english: I still don’t know why the machine isn’t moving.
example.traditional: 我仲未明點解部機唔郁。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung6 mei6 ming4 dim2 gaai2 bou6 gei1 m4 juk1

rows.note: Use 認得 for recognizing a previously encountered person or thing, including telling a familiar face or figure from others.

example.english: Even with a mask on, I still know who you are.
example.traditional: 你戴咗口罩，我都認得你。
example.jyutping: nei5 daai3 zo2 hau2 zaau3 ngo5 dou1 jing6 dak1 nei5
